uncited: Surface-SDF Representation methods reconstruct 3D geometry and appearance by modeling the scene as a continuous implicit surface defined by a Signed Distance Function (SDF), rather than a volumetric density field [6060-neus.md, 10715-volsdf.md].
This approach disentangles geometry from appearance, enabling high-fidelity surface reconstruction and direct mesh extraction [6060-neus.md, 7385-surface-nerf.md].

It differs from standard NeRF-like methods by enforcing geometric consistency through the SDF constraint, and from explicit mesh methods by avoiding explicit mesh extraction during the training phase, instead rendering differentiable images directly from the implicit field [6060-neus.md].

All methods in this family represent scene geometry using a learnable SDF $f(\mathbf{x})$, compute surface normals as $\mathbf{n} = 
abla f(\mathbf{x}) / \|
abla f(\mathbf{x})\|$, and enforce the Eikonal constraint $\|
abla f(\mathbf{x})\| \approx 1$ during training [6060-neus.md, 10715-volsdf.md, 12440-instant-nsr.md].

Volume rendering is performed by converting SDF values into a probability distribution (e.g., via sigmoid or Laplace CDF derivatives) to compute segment alphas and transmittance along rays [6060-neus.md, 10715-volsdf.md, 12440-instant-nsr.md].
NeuS represents a surface as the zero-level set of an SDF and trains it using a novel volume rendering scheme to avoid geometric bias inherent in standard volume rendering [6060-neus.md].

It solves the problem of reconstructing high-quality 3D surfaces from multi-view 2D images by combining the robustness of neural radiance fields with the geometric precision of implicit SDFs [6060-neus.md].

Unlike siblings that also use SDFs, NeuS introduces a specific S-density formulation based on the derivative of the sigmoid function to ensure unbiased surface reconstruction in the first-order approximation [6060-neus.md].
Choose it when high-quality surface reconstruction from multi-view images is needed without explicit mesh extraction during training [6060-neus.md].

VolSDF is a neural inverse rendering method that decouples geometric representation and appearance by modeling scene density as a function of a learnable Signed Distance Function (SDF) [10715-volsdf.md].

It solves the problem of noisy, low-fidelity geometry reconstruction inherent in standard density-based NeRF approaches, where geometry is extracted via arbitrary level sets of generic density functions [10715-volsdf.md].

Unlike siblings that model geometry as a function of density, VolSDF provides a useful inductive bias for geometry, bounds opacity approximation error, and enables efficient unsupervised disentanglement of shape and appearance [10715-volsdf.md].
Choose it when disentanglement of shape and appearance is required, or when stable geometry gradients and opacity error bounds are needed [10715-volsdf.md].
Originated from the integration of neural implicit fields with inverse volume rendering.
VolSDF [10715-volsdf.md] was one of the early works to explicitly model the SDF for volume rendering, aiming to overcome the ambiguity of density-based representations.

NeuS [6060-neus.md] and Surface NeRF [7385-surface-nerf.md] further refined this by introducing specific architectures and optimization strategies (such as hierarchical sampling and alternating optimization) to stabilize training and improve geometric fidelity.
Instant-NSR [12440-instant-nsr.md] later adapted the approach for hash-grid acceleration.

These methods are primarily used in multi-view stereo reconstruction, 3D asset creation, and augmented reality applications where accurate geometry is as important as photorealistic appearance [6060-neus.md, 7385-surface-nerf.md, 10715-volsdf.md, 12440-instant-nsr.md].
